careerShadowScenarios.title: Black Friday Production Outage: Cache Stampede Under Burst Traffic
careerShadowScenarios.context: It is 8:02 PM on Black Friday. Traffic spikes to 25,000 req/sec. The central Redis caching tier evicts hot restaurant catalog keys. Cache miss rate leaps from 2% to 94%. PostgreSQL primary CPU hits 100%, cascading latency to 8,200ms across all checkout APIs. Management asks for immediate triage.
careerShadowScenarios.question: What is your immediate architectural decision to stabilize the system?

options.label: Option A: Spin up 10 extra PostgreSQL Read Replicas
options.feedback: Ineffective: Provisioning replicas takes 8–15 minutes, during which database connections will completely exhaust. Furthermore, read replicas will also get inundated with identical duplicate queries.

options.label: Option B: Deploy Mutex Lock (Singleflight Pattern) on Cache Misses
options.feedback: Optimal Architectural Choice! Singleflight collapses duplicate concurrent cache misses into a single flight query to the primary DB. PostgreSQL CPU immediately stabilizes from 100% to 18%.

options.label: Option C: Flush All Redis Keys to Force Clean Warmup
options.feedback: Catastrophic! Flushing the cache during peak burst traffic shifts 100% of read volume onto an already saturated database, leading to full cluster downtime.

options.label: Option D: Throttle and Drop 85% of Inbound Customer Traffic
options.feedback: Sub-optimal: While it relieves DB pressure, dropping 85% of live checkouts causes massive revenue loss and fails SLA expectations.

careerShadowScenarios.alumnusDebrief: Rohan Mehta (Swiggy Batch '20): 'We actually faced this in 2023! Using Go's golang.org/x/sync/singleflight turned 4,000 duplicate queries for a single IPL match menu into 1 database query. This is a classic interview question!'

careerShadowScenarios.title: Startup Runway Crisis: 3 Weeks of Capital Remaining
careerShadowScenarios.context: Your AI tooling startup has 3 weeks of runway left in bank. Customer churn reached 24% because the self-hosted LLM latency is 4.5s. Two enterprise pilots with banks offer $40,000 ARR each if you deliver an on-premise Dockerized deployment within 10 days.
careerShadowScenarios.question: Where do you allocate 100% of engineering bandwidth?

options.label: Build the on-premise containerized pilot for the 2 enterprise banks to secure immediate cash.
options.feedback: Excellent founder pragmatism! Securing $80,000 immediately extends your runway by 6 months, giving you breathing room to optimize the public product.

options.label: Spend the 3 weeks rewriting the inference pipeline in C++ / CUDA to reduce latency.
options.feedback: High risk of bankruptcy: If the rewrite takes 4 weeks instead of 3, the startup runs out of money before code ever hits production.

careerShadowScenarios.alumnusDebrief: Neha Kapoor (Founder): 'Cash in bank beats theoretical perfection every single time when runway is under 30 days.'

legacyGuides.title: How I Cracked SDE-2 at Swiggy from Tier-2 Campus Without Referrals
keyTakeaways: Stop applying with generic MERN stack to-do apps. Build 1 project that solves network latency or concurrency.
Include unit tests and benchmarking results in your GitHub README; it catches senior engineers' eyes immediately.
In interviews, explain WHY you picked Redis over Memcached or Kafka over RabbitMQ.

legacyGuides.author: Neha Kapoor (HyperScale AI)
legacyGuides.title: 5 Architecture Mistakes College Final-Year Projects Make
keyTakeaways: Over-engineering: Don't use Kubernetes when a single Docker container or VPS is plenty.
Missing metrics: An app without P95 latency graphs doesn't look like production software.
Hardcoded secrets: Always use .env files and clean configuration patterns.
